cards.title: A cosmic water reservoir holds 140 trillion times Earth's oceans
cards.body: Over 12 billion light-years away, a supermassive black hole powering the quasar APM 08279+5255 is surrounded by an enormous vapor cloud. Discovered in 2011, this cosmic reservoir contains roughly 140 trillion times the water in all of Earth's oceans combined. The vapor spans hundreds of light-years in an unusually warm, dense environment, providing astronomers with crucial evidence that water was abundant even in the early universe.

sources.title: Astronomers Find Largest, Most Distant Reservoir of Water

cards.title: NASA never spent millions trying to reinvent the pencil
cards.body: A persistent urban legend claims NASA spent millions developing a zero-gravity pen while Soviet cosmonauts simply used pencils. In reality, both space programs originally used pencils, but snapped graphite leads and flammable wood dust posed serious fire and inhalation risks in pure-oxygen capsules. The pressurized Fisher Space Pen was developed independently by Paul Fisher with his own private funds, and NASA and the Soviets both purchased them at a modest discount.

cards.title: Pluto and its largest moon are frozen in a mutual stare
cards.body: While Earth's Moon is tidally locked to Earth, showing only one face, Earth still rotates beneath it. Pluto and its giant moon Charon take synchronization further: they are mutually tidally locked. Charon takes 6.4 Earth days to orbit Pluto, which is the exact time Pluto takes to rotate once. As a result, Charon never rises or sets—it hovers motionless over a single hemisphere, while the two worlds eternally face each other.

cards.title: Satellites hover permanently motionless at one exact altitude
cards.body: A satellite in geostationary orbit circles Earth at exactly 35,786 kilometers above the equator. At this precise altitude, its orbital velocity matches Earth's rotation rate, taking 23 hours, 56 minutes, and 4 seconds to complete one lap. Because the spacecraft moves in perfect harmony with the ground below, it appears permanently fixed in the sky, allowing ground antennas to stay locked onto television and weather satellites without ever tracking them across the horizon.

cards.title: Jupiter's moon Callisto is the most cratered world known
cards.body: Jupiter's outermost Galilean moon, Callisto, is a frozen relic preserved in time. Unlike worlds shaped by volcanoes, tectonic shifts, or weather, Callisto has had virtually no geological activity to erase its scars for billions of years. Its icy, ancient crust has absorbed meteorite strikes continuously since the birth of the solar system, making it the most heavily cratered object ever discovered. Every new crater on Callisto now almost inevitably overlaps an existing one.

quizzes.question: Roughly how much water does the cloud surrounding quasar APM 08279+5255 contain relative to Earth?
options: About the same as the Atlantic Ocean
Roughly 50 times Earth's oceans
About 140 trillion times Earth's oceans
Nearly 10 billion times the Sun's mass in liquid form
quizzes.explanation: Astronomers found the vapor cloud around APM 08279+5255 holds roughly 140 trillion times the water in all of Earth's oceans combined.

quizzes.question: Why did early space programs avoid using standard pencils in spacecraft cabins?
options: Pencil lead doesn't make contact with paper in microgravity
Graphite debris and wood shavings posed fire and choking hazards
The wood dissolved under the spacecraft cabin's low pressure
Graphite reacts explosively with spaceship window glass
quizzes.explanation: Broken graphite conducted electricity and posed short-circuit fire risks, while floating graphite and wood dust threatened astronaut lungs.

quizzes.question: What is unique about the orbital relationship between Pluto and its largest moon, Charon?
options: Charon orbits Pluto faster than the speed of sound
They are mutually tidally locked and permanently face each other
Charon swaps places with Pluto's second-largest moon every year
Pluto orbits Charon in the opposite direction of its spin
quizzes.explanation: Both bodies are tidally locked to each other, meaning Charon never moves across Pluto's sky and always displays the same face.

quizzes.question: What happens when a satellite reaches geostationary orbit at 35,786 kilometers altitude?
options: It escapes Earth's gravitational pull permanently
Its orbital period matches Earth's rotation, so it appears stationary
It passes over both the North and South Poles on every orbit
Its speed drops to zero relative to deep space
quizzes.explanation: At 35,786 km above the equator, a satellite orbits Earth in exactly one sidereal day, keeping it fixed over one spot on the ground.

quizzes.question: Why is Jupiter's moon Callisto the most heavily cratered body in the solar system?
options: It pulls in comets with a powerful magnetic field
It lacks geological activity like volcanism or tectonics to erase impacts
It orbits directly inside the densest region of the asteroid belt
Its thick carbon dioxide atmosphere attracts meteors
quizzes.explanation: Without internal heat, plate tectonics, or an atmosphere, Callisto has had no geological mechanisms to resurface its crust for billions of years.

guesses.prompt: How many times the water in all Earth's oceans is held in the vapor cloud around quasar APM 08279+5255 (in trillions)?
guesses.explanation: The vapor reservoir around quasar APM 08279+5255 holds roughly 140 trillion times all of Earth's ocean water.

guesses.prompt: At what altitude above Earth's equator must a satellite orbit to remain stationary over one spot on the ground?
guesses.explanation: At exactly 35,786 km, an equatorial satellite completes an orbit in sync with Earth's rotation, holding a fixed position in the sky.

misconceptions.claim: NASA spent millions of taxpayer dollars inventing a zero-gravity pen while the Soviets simply used pencils.
misconceptions.explanation: Both programs initially used pencils until private inventor Paul Fisher funded and developed the pressurized Space Pen on his own dime.

misconceptions.claim: From any location on Pluto's surface, you can watch its giant moon Charon rise and set each day.
misconceptions.explanation: Because Pluto and Charon are mutually tidally locked, Charon hovers eternally over one hemisphere and is completely invisible from the other.

misconceptions.claim: Callisto is covered in craters because its surface has experienced virtually no geological activity to erase them.
misconceptions.explanation: Unlike active worlds, Callisto has had almost no volcanism or tectonic shifting for billions of years, perfectly preserving ancient impact scars.
